title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-sophia-martin
content:
Legal redlines scratchpad - hosting / inference contracts (notes to self)

Context: negotiation with a mid-market customer for a Dedicated + Private combo. They want a lot of custom clauses for data use, telemetry, and indemnity. This is a personal scratchpad for redline points, suggested fallback language, and questions for Legal.

High-level risk buckets to watch
- Data usage & model training: customer asks that Redwood not use any of their request data to train or improve models. We currently have telemetry and aggregate metrics; need explicit carveout.
  - Proposed: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to further train, improve, or tune foundation models or model weights without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service health and performance optimization provided it cannot reasonably be reidentified."
  - Notes: legal may want stronger definition of "de-identified"; might require reference to our Data Processing Addendum (DPA).

- Confidentiality & customer data residency: customer requires data to remain in specific region (EU) and to be purged on termination within 30 days. Also asking for on-prem deployment for sensitive workloads.
  - Check: our Private deployment SLA & purge procedures; can we commit to 30 days? We usually do 90 days for backups.
  - Talking point: offer 30-day purge for live data but 90-day for backups with certification of deletion schedule and optional audit.

- Liability/limitation of liability cap: customer proposes unlimited liability for IP infringement and data breaches. We should push back strongly.
  - Suggested counter: cap = greater of USD 5M or 12 months of fees; carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct and for data breach / regulatory fines limited but not unlimited.
  - Note: for enterprise deals we sometimes negotiate higher caps; flag to Finance if they want to push above standard.

- Indemnity: customer wants Redwood to indemnify for third-party claims arising from use of models (including hallucinations).
  - Concern: impossible to indemnify for output accuracy/hallucinations.
  - Suggested redline: indemnity limited to claims that Redwood materially breached confidentiality, willfully infringed third-party IP in our pre-packaged models, or included malicious code. Exclude indemnity for customer uses and content supplied by customer.

- Security & breach notification: they want 24-hour notification and full forensics report.
  - Our standard: notify within 72 hours for incidents with material impact; provide high-level summary immediately and full report within 30 days.
  - Negotiation point: offer 48-hour initial notification and 30-day forensic report for critical incidents; include SOC2/ISO attestations and option for on-prem log access for audits.

- Audit rights & subcontractors (subprocessing): customer requests quarterly on-site audits and right to approve subprocessors.
  - We normally offer annual audits, certificate sharing (SOC2) and on-demand audits with NDA/cost sharing. Approve subprocessors but do not require per-subprocessor customer approval.
  - Proposed language: annual attestation + on-demand audit (reasonable notice and cost reimbursement). Subprocessor list to be provided; for new high-risk subprocessors we'll notify in advance and allow exit for material objections.

- Export controls & sanctions: customer wants Redwood to be responsible for all downstream export compliance.
  - We can warrant we comply with applicable export laws and will not provide Services in sanctioned countries. Do not accept open-ended downstream compliance guarantees.

- IP ownership and outputs: customer wants full ownership of outputs and that Redwood has no rights to models or generated content.
  - Standard: grant of ownership to Customer for Customer Content and outputs generated from Customer Content. Redwood retains underlying model IP and rights to pre-existing tools.
  - Propose: explicit language: "Customer owns Customer Content and output generated solely from Customer Content. Redwood retains all rights to models, model improvements, and service-level telemetry." Offer a narrow license back for aggregated/de-identified telemetry only.

- Performance SLAs & remedies: they want credits + termination right for missed latency SLOs.
  - Our standard: credits up to a % of monthly fees; termination only for repeated SLA breaches after cure period.
  - Negotiation: accept credits and one-time termination right if SLA missed N times in a quarter with 30-day cure window. Avoid immediate termination for 1-off incidents.

Redline checklist (quick)
- [ ] Explicit non-training clause for customer data (proposed language above)
- [ ] Data residency + purge timelines (confirm backup policy)
- [ ] Limitation of liability cap defined and carved
- [ ] Indemnity scope narrowed (no hallucinations)
- [ ] Security incident SLAs (48-72h negotiation)
- [ ] Audit rights: annual + on-demand with cost share
- [ ] Subprocessor notification process
- [ ] Export/sanctions compliance warranty only
- [ ] Ownership of outputs vs model IP clarified
- [ ] SLA remedies: credits + cure period before termination

Open questions / legal to review
- Does Legal want the exact "de-identified" definition in the DPA, or is the DPA sufficient?
- Are we comfortable committing to a 30-day live-data purge if backups are 90 days? Should we offer a certified 30-day option at additional fee?
- For indemnity: can we add an explicit carveout for misuse by customer (including fine-tuning, sharing outputs) that causes third-party claims?
- Is the suggested cap (greater of $5M or 12 months fees) within standard playbook or do we need CRO sign-off?
- For telemetry: can we add a customer-controlled opt-out for telemetry collection on Dedicated/Private? (Product ask: for Dedicated we can turn off telemetry; for Private need to confirm.)

Negotiation talking points (for AE / AM to use)
- "We are committed to keeping your data private: we will not use your content to train our global models without explicit consent, and we can provide a DPA that describes de-identification safeguards."
- "For high-sensitivity workloads we can provide Private deployment and regionally isolated infrastructure; we can also offer 30-day live data purge and documented backup deletion schedule."
- "We can accept reasonable audit rights and SOC2 evidence; for ad-hoc audits we ask for reimbursement of costs and reasonable notice to coordinate."
- "Limitation of liability: our suggested cap protects both parties and lets us scale sustainably - higher caps are possible for enterprise commitments but need Finance/legal approval."

Action items (next steps)
- [ ] Send this draft to Legal (cc: Noah, Maya) with flagged sections for IP/indemnity and de-identification definition.
- [ ] Confirm backup retention/restore timelines with infra (ticket: ENG-789).
- [ ] Determine if Dedicated telemetry can be disabled (ask infra team).
- [ ] Prepare counterparty-friendly redline with proposed language to hand to AE.

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. Capture Legal feedback into Confluence page and then replace with final template language. Save negotiated language per region (EU vs US) because data residency/export clauses vary.

End of scratchpad.
